lsr.rule: I obtain and follow a permit before hot work, confined-space entry, excavation, electrical, critical lifts or radiography.
do: Understand the hazards and controls on the permit
Confirm isolations and gas tests are done
Stop if conditions change
never: Start without a signed permit
Continue after expiry

lsr.rule: I obtain authorisation before overriding or disabling safety-critical equipment.
do: Treat guards, interlocks, alarms, trips and limit switches as life-critical
Use the override register with time limit and compensating measures
never: Remove a guard to keep production going
Disable a reversing alarm or LMI

lsr.rule: I verify isolation and zero energy before work begins.
do: Isolate, lock, tag, release stored energy, test for dead
Apply my own lock; keep my key
never: Trust a stop button or closed valve as isolation
Remove someone else's lock

lsr.rule: I enter a confined space only with a permit, a tested atmosphere and an attendant.
do: Gas-test before and during; continuous ventilation
Keep the retrieval line attached
never: Enter to rescue without breathing apparatus
Leave the attendant post

lsr.rule: I protect myself against a fall when working at height.
do: Use guardrails, nets or covers first; harness to a rated anchor otherwise
Inspect harness and lanyard before use
never: Tie off to scaffold tubes or rebar
Work on a red-tagged scaffold or fragile roof

lsr.rule: I plan lifts and control the area.
do: Lift plan, certified gear, trained operator and signaller
Barricade the zone; tag lines on loads
never: Walk or work under a suspended load
Exceed the load chart or lift in high wind

lsr.rule: I keep myself and others out of the line of fire.
do: Position away from moving plant, swing radius, tension ropes, pinch points, stored energy
Use barriers and spotters
never: Stand between a reversing vehicle and a fixed object
Put hands where you cannot see

do: Seat belt, speed limit, banksman for reversing, journey management for long trips
Daily pre-start check
never: Use a phone while driving
Drive fatigued or under the influence

lsr.rule: I control flammables and ignition sources.
do: Permit, gas test, fire watch, extinguisher within reach
Clear combustibles 11 m or protect
never: Weld or grind near fuel, cylinders or open drains without a permit
Leave hot work without a fire watch

lsr.rule: I never enter an unprotected trench.
do: Shoring, sloping or box beyond 1.5 m; permit-to-dig; daily inspection
Spoil and plant ≥ 1 m from edge
never: Dig near marked services without hand-digging
Work below undermined ground

lsr.rule: I arrive fit for work and wear the right PPE.
do: Report fatigue, illness, medication that affects alertness
Wear and inspect PPE for the task
never: Work under the influence of alcohol or drugs
Remove PPE in a hazard zone

lsr.rule: I stop any work I believe is unsafe and report hazards, near misses and injuries.
do: Use stop-work authority without fear of blame
Report within the shift
never: Hide an injury or near miss
Restart until the issue is resolved by the supervisor

items: No entry without induction, ID card and gate registration; visitors escorted
Follow signs, barricades, tags and instructions of marshals; never remove a barricade or tag
No alcohol, drugs or intoxicated persons; random testing may apply
No smoking except in designated areas; no open flames in camps
No mobile phones while operating plant, driving, walking in plant zones or at height
No horseplay, running, fighting or weapons
Working hours and rest as per roster; no double shifts without approval
Children not permitted on site or in work areas; no under-18 in hazardous work
Minimum: helmet with chin strap, safety boots, hi-vis — always
Task PPE per permit/method statement (harness, goggles, face shield, gloves, respirator, hearing protection)
Inspect PPE daily; replace damaged PPE free of charge
Long trousers and sleeves in chemical, welding and hot-metal areas; no synthetic clothing for hot work
Tight-fitting respirators require a clean-shaven face
No work without a risk assessment/method statement and a daily toolbox talk
Permits for hot work, confined space, excavation, electrical, WAH, lifting (critical), radiography
Lockout before maintenance; test for dead
Keep out of the line of fire; never under suspended loads
Work at height only with collective protection or 100% tie-off
Trenches > 1.5 m shored; ladders within 7.5 m
Use the right tool, inspected and guarded; no modifications
Chemicals labelled, SDS known, stored by compatibility; no decanting to food containers
Housekeeping: clean as you go; walkways and exits clear; waste segregated
Weather rules: stop WAH/lifting at wind > 40 km/h or lightning; heat-level work restrictions
Only authorised, licensed and trained operators; daily pre-start checks
Site speed limit 10–20 km/h; seat belts; banksman for reversing; no passengers on plant
Lifting gear certified and colour-coded; no homemade attachments
Gas cylinders upright, chained, capped; flashback arrestors
Electrical equipment via RCD-protected industrial sockets; damaged cables tagged out
Keys removed from unattended plant; loads lowered; machines isolated at shift end
Drink water every 15–20 min in heat; use rest shelters
Report injuries, however small, to the first-aider the same shift
Use toilets and washing facilities; wash before eating; no eating in chemical/dust areas
Medical examinations as scheduled for dangerous operations
Report fatigue or illness; don't work when unfit
No burning of waste; segregate waste; hazardous waste to the designated store
No discharge of oil, chemicals, silt or sewage to drains or land
Dust suppression and covered transport; no idling of plant
Noise limits and timing for night work respected
Know the alarm, assembly point, emergency numbers and nearest extinguisher/first-aid
Raise the alarm first; fight fire only if trained and safe
Never use lifts in a fire; never re-enter until all-clear
Report to your supervisor at the assembly point for head-count

standing.purpose: Every person has the authority and duty to stop any work they believe is unsafe, without fear of reprisal.
steps: Stop: say 'STOP WORK' clearly; make the area safe (do not leave equipment in a dangerous state)
Notify: tell the supervisor/permit holder what you saw and why it is unsafe
Investigate: supervisor and safety officer assess; correct the condition or change the method
Resume: only when the hazard is controlled and the crew is re-briefed; the person who stopped the work is thanked and the event is logged
Follow-up: record in the stop-work register; trend monthly; recognise good calls; discipline retaliation

standing.purpose: Formal written control for high-risk, non-routine work.
steps: Request with JSA; issuer walks down the site with the receiver
Isolations, gas tests, precautions and rescue arrangements completed and recorded
Both sign; permit displayed at the job and the control point; crew briefed and signed
Validity ≤ one shift; suspend on alarms or changed conditions; re-validate with re-check
Close-out inspection by issuer; de-isolation only after closure; file

standing.purpose: Zero-energy state before any work on equipment.
steps: Identify all energy sources from the ECP
Shut down; isolate; lock and tag each point (personal lock); group lock box for crews
Release stored energy; block/support
Test for dead/zero energy (try-start, proved tester, gauges)
Work; shift handover with lock transfer; restore only by lock owners after head-count

standing.purpose: Align the crew on the day's tasks, hazards, controls and permit conditions.
steps: Supervisor gathers crew at start of shift (10–15 min) at the workface
Cover: tasks, hazards from JSA, permits, PPE, weather, emergency arrangements, lessons from yesterday
Ask questions; invite concerns; confirm understanding in the crew's language
Record topic and attendance (signatures); file with the permit
Repeat for new crews joining mid-shift or when the task changes

standing.purpose: Capture every unsafe act/condition, near miss and injury so it can be fixed before it hurts someone.
steps: Anyone can report: verbally to supervisor, observation card, QR/app, or safety officer — within the shift
No-blame rule for reporting; anonymous option available
Safety officer classifies (unsafe act/condition/near miss/injury) and assigns action with owner and date
High-potential near misses investigated like injuries (RCA within 72 h)
Feedback to the reporter; monthly trend review at the safety committee; recognise top reporters

standing.purpose: Structured observation of work practices with immediate feedback.
steps: Observer (trained; supervisor/peer) announces the observation; observes 10–15 min using the unsafe-acts/conditions categories
Stops imminent danger immediately; otherwise completes the observation
Gives feedback: recognise safe behaviour first, then discuss at-risk behaviour and barriers (why?)
Records on the observation card (no names for behaviours; names for recognition only)
Safety team trends categories weekly; removes barriers (equipment, procedure, training); publishes results

standing.purpose: Visible leadership and verification of controls.
steps: Site head/manager walks a defined area weekly with the safety officer
Talks to workers about their task, hazards and what would make it safer
Checks a sample: permits, PPE, housekeeping, isolation, emergency equipment
Records findings with owners/dates; closes last walk's actions
Shares positives and lessons at the next safety meeting

standing.purpose: Keep visitors safe and out of hazardous areas.
steps: Register at gate; ID; brief on site rules, emergency, PPE; sign visitor induction
Issue PPE; escort at all times; restricted-area access only with permit holder
Vehicles parked outside work zones; no photography in restricted areas unless approved
Sign out; PPE returned; emergency head-count includes visitors

standing.purpose: Prevent road and site vehicle incidents.
steps: Licensed, fit drivers; vehicle inspected; seat belts for all; speed limits; no phones
Journey plan for trips > 2 h or at night: route, rest stops every 2 h, max 10 h driving/day, check-in calls
No driving 11 pm–5 am for long trips unless approved; fatigue management
Loads secured/covered; tippers never travel raised
Incident: stop, make safe, first aid, report to supervisor and police as required

standing.purpose: Zero tolerance for impairment at work.
steps: No alcohol or illegal drugs on site; prescription medication affecting alertness to be declared
Random and for-cause testing where policy applies (breath test at gate)
Impaired person removed from work safely (not sent home alone if unsafe); recorded
Support/referral for dependency; disciplinary action per policy
Contractors bound by the same rule
Wind > 40 km/h (or crane limit ≈ 9–10 m/s): stop WAH on exposed areas, crane lifts, sheeting; secure loose materials
Lightning within 10 km / thunder heard: stop WAH, crane, scaffold, roof, water and electrical work; shelter in buildings/vehicles; resume 30 min after last thunder
Heavy rain / flood warning: stop excavation entry, inspect after; divert runoff; pump readiness; stop electrical outdoor work
Heat level red (IMD/WBGT): no heavy outdoor work at peak hours; water/rest/shade; buddy system
Cyclone warning (TN coast): secure cranes, lower loads, evacuate workers from low-lying camps, follow TNSDMA orders
Dense fog/smoke: restrict vehicle movement, lights on, marshals

standing.purpose: Extra controls when supervision and rescue are reduced.
steps: Task list approved for night; no prohibited lone tasks (confined space, WAH, HT, hot work)
Lighting ≥ 50 lux general / 100–200 lux task; class 3 hi-vis
Supervisor, first-aider and ERT member on shift; emergency vehicle available
Lone worker check-in every 1–2 h; escalation if missed
Women night shift: consent, transport with security, CCTV, batch size per state rules

standing.purpose: Prevent injuries from stored pressure energy.
steps: Written test procedure; hydrotest preferred; pneumatic only with engineering approval and exclusion zone
Calibrated gauges (2), relief valve set ≤ 110% test pressure, vent lines
Barricade; nobody in line of flanges/plugs; pressurise in stages with holds; inspect at reduced pressure
Depressurise and drain before any adjustment; never tighten under pressure
Record test; release permit
Any change to process, equipment, chemical, layout, procedure, people or temporary works raises an MoC
Risk assessment; documents updated; approvals; training
Pre-start-up safety review; temporary changes time-limited
Close and audit

standing.purpose: Same standard for everyone on site.
steps: Pre-qualify; contract HSE clauses; licences, insurance, worker registration
Induct every worker; approve method statements; verify equipment certificates
Daily toolbox talks; joint inspections; stop-work authority
Monthly scorecard; non-conformance notices; demobilisation close-out

standing.purpose: Protect people, preserve evidence, meet legal clocks.
steps: Rescue, first aid, 108/112; isolate hazards; stop adjacent work
Preserve scene for fatal/serious incidents; photos; witnesses
Internal report within 1 h; statutory notices per the Incident navigator (death forthwith; others 12 h; MSIHC 48 h; electrical 48 h; boiler 24 h)
Investigate (RCA ≤ 72 h); CAPA; lessons shared

standing.purpose: Respond to violations fairly, distinguishing error from recklessness.
steps: Classify: unintentional error / at-risk shortcut tolerated by system / reckless disregard (just-culture test)
Error → coach and fix the system; at-risk → coach, remove incentive, re-train; reckless → disciplinary ladder (verbal, written, suspension, removal)
Life-Saving Rule breaches: removal from site pending investigation; supervisors accountable for tolerance
Recognise and reward safe behaviour and reporting equally visibly
Record consistently; review for fairness; apply to contractors and staff alike
Raise the alarm: shout 'FIRE', break-glass/manual call point; call 101/112 and the control room
If trained and the fire is small: fight it with the correct extinguisher (PASS – pull, aim, squeeze, sweep), keeping an exit behind you
Otherwise evacuate: nearest exit, no lifts, close doors behind you, help others; stop plant/isolate gas and power if safe
Go to the assembly point; report to your supervisor for head-count; report missing persons to the incident controller
Do not re-enter until the all-clear; ERT receives the fire brigade with the site plan and chemical inventory
Stop work; make equipment safe (lower loads, isolate, stop vehicles) only if it takes seconds
Leave by the nearest safe route; walk; help injured and visitors; no lifts
Move to the assembly point upwind (toxic release) or away from the structure (collapse); alternative point if primary is unsafe
Head-count by supervisor/contractor; report missing persons; wait for instructions
Re-entry only on the incident controller's all-clear

emergency.trigger: Collapse, severe bleeding, unconsciousness, major injury
steps: Danger: make the scene safe (isolate power, stop plant); call for the first-aider and 108/112; send someone to guide the ambulance
Response & airway: check response; open airway; check breathing (≤ 10 s)
Not breathing: start CPR 30:2 and send for the AED; breathing but unconscious: recovery position
Control severe bleeding with direct pressure; treat shock; keep the casualty warm; nothing by mouth
Record time, actions, vital signs; hand over to ambulance (MIST: mechanism, injuries, signs, treatment); preserve the scene; notify per incident protocol

emergency.trigger: Gas alarm, odour, visible cloud, detector reading
steps: Raise the toxic-gas alarm; stop ignition sources (flammable) and hot work
Move upwind/crosswind to the assembly point; use escape respirators; do not run through the cloud
Non-ERT persons indoors: shelter-in-place (close doors/windows, stop AC, go to upper floors), await instructions
ERT only (SCBA, suits) isolates the source and applies the emergency kit; scrubber/water curtain as appropriate
Head-count; medical triage; notify fire service, police, District authority and neighbours as per the off-site plan; MSIHC 48-h report

emergency.trigger: Loss of containment to ground, drain or water
steps: Alert; isolate the source if safe (close valve, upright drum); remove ignition sources
PPE per SDS; contain with booms/absorbents/sand; block drains
Collect into labelled containers as hazardous waste; decontaminate area and PPE
Report: internal; SPCB forthwith for significant/off-site releases (HOWM Form 11; EP Act s.9)
Investigate and fix the cause (bund, valve, procedure)

emergency.trigger: Person in contact with electricity, electric shock, arc flash
steps: Do NOT touch the casualty until the supply is isolated; switch off at the source or use a dry non-conductive object (LV only); HT: keep 10+ m away and call the utility/control room to isolate
Once safe: check response and breathing; CPR/AED if not breathing (electrical arrest responds well to defibrillation)
Treat burns (entry/exit wounds) by cooling and covering; treat for shock; immobilise if thrown/fallen
All electric-shock casualties to hospital for cardiac monitoring, even if they feel fine
Isolate and preserve the equipment; notify Electrical Inspector within 48 h (fatal: immediately)

emergency.trigger: Worker fallen or hanging in harness
steps: Call for rescue team and 108; do not let the suspended person hang: rescue within 10–15 min (MEWP, rescue kit, ladder, lower by controlled descent)
While waiting, tell them to move legs, push against a surface or stand in foot loops to keep blood circulating
After rescue, assess ABC; treat injuries; spinal precautions if fall > 2 m or mechanism suggests; lay flat and monitor (HSE: upright positioning no longer advised)
Fallen to ground: do not move unless in danger; stabilise head/neck; control bleeding; keep warm
Hospital for all falls > 2 m and all suspension events; retire the harness/lanyard; investigate

emergency.trigger: Entrant collapsed, alarm, loss of communication
steps: Attendant raises the alarm and calls the rescue team; does NOT enter
Attempt non-entry rescue: retrieval line/winch, ventilation to maximum, pass breathing air if available
Entry rescue only by trained team with SCBA and a second attendant; continuous gas monitoring
Once out: CPR/AED/oxygen as needed; treat for toxic exposure (hospital, SDS)
Preserve the space; investigate (atmosphere, isolation, permit); dangerous-occurrence notice 12 h
Evacuate the area and adjacent structures; sound the alarm; stop cranes and vehicles
Head-count immediately; identify trapped persons by last known location
Do not enter unstable debris; rescue only when the engineer/ERT confirms stability or with fire service USAR; shore as you go
First aid to the accessible injured; crush-injury precautions (medical team before releasing persons trapped > 15 min)
Preserve the scene; notify 12 h as dangerous occurrence; structural engineer review before any re-entry

emergency.trigger: Trench wall failure with persons inside
steps: Call 112/101/108; stop plant; keep everyone away from the edge — secondary collapse is likely
Do not jump in; locate the victim; if the head is clear, keep airway open and give air (hose/ventilation)
Dig by hand from the side with shoring installed progressively; never use the excavator near the victim
Treat crush/asphyxia on release; hospital
Dangerous-occurrence notice 12 h; investigate protective system failure

emergency.t: Crane Overturn / Dropped Load / Contact with Power Line
emergency.trigger: Crane instability, load drop, boom contact with lines
steps: Clear the area; stop all other lifts; operator stays in cab if the crane contacts a live line (jump clear with feet together only if the crane is on fire)
Power line contact: keep everyone ≥ 10 m away; call the utility to de-energise; treat the ground as live
Casualties: first aid once the scene is safe; 108
Secure the crane (engineer/OEM); do not attempt to right it without a plan
Notify dangerous occurrence within 12 h; preserve LMI data and certificates
Stop traffic; cones/marshals; switch off engines; fire risk check (fuel)
First aid: do not move casualties unless in danger; control bleeding; CPR if needed; 108
Pinned person: stabilise the vehicle (chocks/crane) before any lifting; medical team present for crush > 15 min
Police (100) for public-road accidents; preserve the scene; breath tests per policy
Report to RTO/insurer; internal investigation; dangerous occurrence if on site with injury
Shout, throw a lifebuoy/line, keep eyes on the person; do not jump in unless trained with a flotation aid
Rescue boat/reach aid; pull the person out horizontally if possible
Not breathing: 5 rescue breaths then CPR 30:2 (breaths are vital in drowning); AED; remove wet clothes, keep warm
Breathing: recovery position; monitor; all submersion victims to hospital (delayed lung injury)
Coast guard 1554 for sea; report

emergency.trigger: Confusion, collapse, hot skin, no sweating, temperature > 40 °C
steps: Call 108; move to shade; remove outer clothing
Cool aggressively: immerse in cool water, or douse with water and fan, ice packs to neck/armpits/groin; continue until help arrives
Conscious: sips of water/ORS; unconscious: recovery position, nothing by mouth
Monitor breathing; CPR if needed
Record heat level and work pattern; review schedule and acclimatisation

emergency.trigger: Bite marks, swelling, pain, drooping eyelids, difficulty swallowing/breathing
steps: Do it R.I.G.H.T.: Reassure; Immobilise the limb (splint, keep still, below heart level); Get to hospital with antivenom (108); Tell the doctor the symptoms
Remove rings, watches, tight clothing; note the time; photograph the snake only if safe — do not try to catch it
Do NOT: cut, suck, apply a tourniquet, ice, electric shock, herbal remedies, or give alcohol
Monitor breathing; if breathing weakens (neurotoxic), support with bag-valve mask if trained
Record; check the area for snakes; remove debris/rodent attractants
Stop WAH, crane, scaffold, roof, electrical and water work; evacuate open areas, tall structures, trees, metal fences
Shelter in a building or closed metal vehicle; avoid phone lines, plumbing, open windows
If caught outside: crouch low with feet together away from tall objects; do not lie flat
Struck person: safe to touch; CPR/AED immediately (cardiac arrest is reversible); treat burns; hospital
Resume 30 min after the last thunder

emergency.trigger: IMD warning, rising water, state DMA alert
steps: Activate the weather plan: secure cranes (free slew), lower loads, lash materials, stop WAH
Evacuate low-lying areas and camps to designated shelters; cut power to flood-prone DBs
Check excavations and cofferdams; pumps on; keep people out until inspected
Account for all persons; communication with district control room (1077)
After: inspect scaffolds, excavations, electrical and structures before resuming; snake/disease precautions
Indoors: DROP, COVER, HOLD ON under a sturdy table; away from glass; do not run outside during shaking; no lifts
Outdoors: move away from structures, scaffolds, cranes, lines; crouch
Plant operators: stop, lower loads, stay in cab until shaking stops
After: evacuate to open assembly point; expect aftershocks; check for gas leaks, fires, structural damage; do not re-enter until inspected
Head-count; first aid; report
Threat call: stay calm, note exact words, caller details, background sounds, time; do not hang up; alert security/site head
Do not touch or move suspicious objects; do not use radios/phones within 25 m
Evacuate as directed (route away from the object); assembly point at a safe distance
Police (100/112) and bomb squad; hand over information; follow their instructions
Return only on police all-clear; debrief
Security secures gates; non-essential workers withdrawn to safe area; no confrontation
Inform police (100) and site head; protect lives first, property second
Safe shutdown of hazardous processes if the site may be entered; isolate fuel/chemicals; secure explosives
Account for persons; medical aid; record events (CCTV)
Management/HR engage through recognised channels; resume on police advice
Emergency lighting and DG start; check critical loads (fire pumps, ventilation, hoists, confined-space fans)
Stop confined-space work if ventilation lost; evacuate; stop hot work in process areas if F&G lost
Persons in lifts/hoists: communicate; rescue by trained persons
Treat all circuits as live for restoration; check interlocks before restart
Log and investigate
Evacuate; expect secondary explosions and fire; move upwind
Alarm; 112/101/108; ERT only with PPE assesses
Isolate fuel, gas, electricity if safe; account for persons
Triage casualties (blast lung, burns, fragments); hospital
Preserve the scene; dangerous occurrence 12 h; MSIHC 48 h
Clear the area; extend the cordon (survey meter boundary 1 µSv/h or as RSO directs)
Only RSO/qualified radiographers approach; retrieval with tongs/shielding; never touch a source
Lost source: secure the area, call AERB and police immediately; search with meters
Exposed persons: record dose, medical evaluation
Report to AERB within 24 h; investigate
Cool with cool running water for 20 min (start immediately; effective up to 3 h); leave adhered bitumen/metal on skin
Remove clothing/jewellery not stuck to the burn; cover with cling film or non-fluffy dressing; keep warm
No ice, butter, toothpaste, ointments; do not burst blisters
Call 108 for burns larger than the palm, face/hands/genitals, full thickness, inhalation or electrical burns
Burns-centre tie-up; record; investigate

emergency.trigger: Cluster of fever/respiratory cases; health authority alert
steps: Isolate symptomatic persons; masks; medical assessment; inform District Health Officer
Screening at gate; hygiene stations; ventilation; stagger shifts; limit gatherings
Contact tracing; quarantine arrangements in camp; sanitisation
Follow MoHFW/State advisories; communicate daily in local languages
Record; review welfare and camp density
